item.title: Notetaker 0.1.0 beta 8
item.description:
Eighth beta. Type your own notes during a meeting, and Notetaker writes notes that cover them. Dutch meetings now get Dutch notes and use your personal dictionary. Beta 7 finds it within a day and asks to restart.
## What changed
- **Your notes (D43).** While a session records, the live page has a "Your notes" field. Type a few rough words there. - The notes Notetaker writes cover each of your points that the meeting supports. A point the meeting does not hold stays out of the notes. - Notetaker saves your text while you type, so a crash keeps it. It is in search, on the session page above the written notes, and in the export under "My notes". - Notetaker reads the first 300 words. Above that, the field says "The notes use your first 300 words." - When Notetaker stops a session by itself after a long silence, the last words you typed still count. - **Each note links to its source (D43).** A decision, an action item or an open question shows the transcript line it came from. A note with no clear source has no link. - **Copy notes (D43).** "Copy notes" on a session page, to the right of Export, or Shift Command C, puts the notes on the pasteboard as Markdown: the same text as the export, without the transcript. - **Dutch notes for a Dutch meeting (D45).** The summary and every note of a meeting in Nederlands are in Dutch. - **Your personal dictionary reaches Dutch transcripts (D46).** A second small model finds the dictionary words in the audio and corrects the transcript. The Dutch download is now 570 MB. If you already have the Dutch model, the extra 98 MB comes at the next launch or language pick. - **Dictionary words stay out of the notes when nobody said them.** The note writer gets only the dictionary words that the meeting holds. - **The menu says when the Dutch model gets ready.** When the load takes longer than 3 s, the menu shows "Preparing the speech model for Nederlands". - **Fewer invented notes.** An open question that the meeting answers, or does not hold, is dropped. An action item no longer gets a due date such as "not named". - **Numbers in your notes.** "12" in your notes and "twelve" in the transcript count as the same word. - **The export date is the same on every Mac.** For example: `2025-10-16 11:00, 32 min`. - **The meeting prompt banner** has the size of its card again.
## What to try
- In a meeting, type three or four points in "Your notes". After Stop, check that the notes cover them. - Click the link of a decision and check that the transcript line says it. - Add a name to your personal dictionary, and record a Dutch meeting that says it.
## Known gaps
- An action item can still go to "Speaker 2" when the sentence names the person (D44). - Your notes are not tested in a real call yet.

item.title: Notetaker 0.1.0 beta 7
item.description:
Seventh beta. Notetaker now writes Dutch transcripts, and Stop no longer hangs. Beta 6 finds it within a day and asks to restart.
## What changed
- **Dutch transcripts (D40).** A new menu item, "Transcript language", has English and Nederlands. - The choice holds for the next session. During a recording it also switches the session that records now. The words from before the switch stay. - Nederlands uses the Parakeet speech model on the Mac. The model is 470 MB. It downloads once, when you pick Nederlands, and the first load takes about 40 s. The audio stays on the Mac. - English stays on Apple's speech engine, which uses your personal dictionary. - **Read again (D40).** A session's page has a "Read again" menu: "Read again in English" or "Read again in Nederlands". It reads the stored audio again in that language and writes the notes again. The speakers and the names you gave stay. Use it for a meeting that was recorded in the wrong language, while its audio is still on the Mac (30 days). - **Stop no longer hangs (D36).** A session could stay in "finalizing" for good. Stop now always ends, and each finalizing step has a deadline that grows with the length of the audio. - **Sessions that a crash stopped are finished at the next launch (D38).** Notetaker reads them again from their audio. After two failed tries, the session shows as failed. - **A silent system lane is reported (D36).** When a call app plays but the system lane records only silence for 30 s, the session shows a failure line, and Notetaker tries a new audio tap. - **Teams names come back in new Teams builds (D37).** The roster and the speaking cues work again in Teams 26261. - **Lane audio uses half the disk (D39).** The lane files are now 16-bit. - **Notetaker measures itself (D36).** `metrics.jsonl` holds one line per measure for about a month: times, counts, memory, states. It never holds a name or a word. "Save diagnostics" adds it to the folder. - **App Nap** stays off during a session, so a long meeting is not slowed down.
## What to try
- Pick Nederlands in "Transcript language", wait for the download, and record a Dutch meeting. - Open an old Dutch meeting that came out as English, and choose "Read again in Nederlands". - In a Teams call, check that the speakers get names. If not, choose "Save diagnostics" and send the folder.
## Known gaps
- The personal dictionary does not reach a Dutch transcript yet. - The notes of a Dutch meeting are not measured yet. The note prompts are in English. - While the Dutch model loads for the first time, the menu does not say so. - Words from the personal dictionary can show up in the notes as if the meeting said them. - An action item can go to "Speaker 2" when the sentence names the person. - The meeting prompt banner is too tall.

item.title: Notetaker 0.1.0 beta 6
item.description:
Sixth beta. Notetaker now names speakers from what the people in the meeting call each other. Beta 5 finds it within a day and asks to restart.
## What changed
- **Names from name calls (D35).** When a voice has no name after the voiceprints and the Teams names, Notetaker reads the transcript for three things: - An introduction: "I'm Mark", "My name's Priya" or "Ik ben Sanne" names the voice that says it. - A call: "Anna, what do you think?" points at the next voice. A voice needs two calls in two turns, and all calls on that voice must give the same name. - A thanks: "Thanks, Anna" supports a name that a call gave. A thanks never gives a name alone. - Only the names of attendees count: the people in the calendar event and the people in the Teams call. - A name call never changes a name that a voiceprint or Teams gave. - This works in Zoom, Google Meet, Teams in a browser and Teams in another language. In those calls, the Teams names give nothing. - **The naming log line** counts the name calls by kind, and the voices they named. When the name calls name nobody, a second line says why. As in beta 5, the log holds counts, not names.
## What to try
- Record a meeting where the people call each other by name, in any call app. Put the meeting in the calendar with its attendees, so that Notetaker knows the names. - After Stop, look at the speaker names. A wrong name: rename the speaker. Then choose "Save diagnostics" and send `log.txt`. The lines that start with `Naming:` show what each step did.
## Known gaps
- The name calls were tested on 44 meetings that were written by hand, not recorded. On those meetings they gave no wrong name and named 74 % of the voices. Real meetings can give a wrong name. Rename it, and tell us the sentence that caused it. - A person whose name is said only once usually stays a number. - Name calls work in English and Dutch only. - People who are not on the Teams stage give no Teams names. Name calls can still name them. - A guest line heard through the speakers can still show as "Me".

item.title: Notetaker 0.1.0 beta 5
item.description:
Fifth beta. When the Teams names do not appear, Notetaker now tells you which step failed. Beta 4 finds it within a day and asks to restart.
## What changed
- **Every step that names a speaker logs.** Notetaker writes a line when it finds a Teams call, when it sees who speaks, and when it names the voices at the end. When a step fails, the line says why: no Accessibility access, no call found, a tile it does not know, no speaking ring, or cues that named nobody. The log holds counts and states, not names (D34). - **"Save diagnostics" in the menu.** It writes a folder with the app and Mac facts, the log of this run, and, while Teams runs, ten copies of the Teams window. The folder opens in the Finder. Nothing leaves the Mac: you read the files and decide what to send.
## What to try
- Record a Teams call. While somebody speaks, choose "Save diagnostics" in the menu. It takes some seconds. Send `about.txt` and `log.txt` from the folder. `teams.json` holds the names in the call and any open chat text: read it before you send it. - After Stop, choose "Save diagnostics" again. The log then also holds the naming step.
## Known gaps
- The new logging is not yet tested in a live Teams call. - Teams in a language other than English, and Teams in a web browser, give no names. The log now says so. - People who are not on the Teams stage give no speaker names. - A guest line heard through the speakers can still show as "Me".

item.title: Notetaker 0.1.0 beta 4
item.description:
Fourth beta. Notetaker now knows who you talk to in a Microsoft Teams call, and who says what. Beta 3 finds it within a day and asks to restart.
## What changed
- **Names from Teams.** During a Teams call, Notetaker reads the Teams window on your Mac. The people on the stage become the attendees of the session, and a person who joins late is added. The meeting title names a session that has no calendar event. No bot joins the call, and nothing leaves the Mac (D33). - **A name on each line.** Teams shows who speaks. Notetaker reads that once a second, and at the end it gives each line of the call audio the name of the person who spoke it. The action items in the notes now have real owners. - **Access on a click only.** Choose "Name the people in Teams calls" in the menu, then turn on Notetaker in System Settings > Privacy & Security > Accessibility. Without this access, sessions work as in beta 3. - **"Check for updates" works again after a download.** While a downloaded update waited for the restart, the menu item did nothing. It now shows the update window again.
## What to try
- Give Notetaker the Accessibility access. Record a Teams call with two colleagues. At the end, the attendees and each line of their speech carry their names, and the action items name their owners.
## Known gaps
- Tested in a live Teams call with two synthetic voices, not yet with real people. - Teams in a language other than English, and Teams in a web browser, give no names. - People who are not on the Teams stage give no speaker names. - A guest line heard through the speakers can still show as "Me".
